scenes.heading: Naming
scenes.caption: Naming is the choice of labels in code, files, and APIs. The label is part of the design, because it is what people read first. A review that argues about names is often a review about meaning. If you cannot name it, you do not know what it is yet.

scenes.heading: functions
scenes.caption: Functions are named blocks of steps. You call them with inputs, they run, and they can return a result. They are the unit of explanation in a program. If you can name a function well, you understand the job.

scenes.heading: Comments
scenes.caption: A comment is a note in the source that the program does not run. It should say why, not repeat what the next line already says. Comments that restate the code go stale and then lie. A comment that explains a constraint saves the next person from “fixing” it.

items: A comment is a note in the source that the program does not run
It should say why, not repeat what the next line already says
Comments that restate the code go stale and then lie. A comment that explains a constraint saves the next person from “fixing” it

scenes.heading: Step by step: Comments
scenes.caption: Do not comment name = name + 1. Do comment a rule that is not visible, such as a limit imposed by another system. Delete comments that no longer match the code. Prefer a clearer name over a comment that translates a bad one.

scenes.heading: formatting
scenes.caption: Formatting means turning values into text a person will read, or laying code out so a person can read it. Say which one you are doing. Pretty output is not sanitising. Building a query or a command by formatting untrusted text is how injection bugs happen.

scenes.heading: State
scenes.caption: State is data a component remembers, and when it changes the component renders again. Props come from the parent. State belongs to the component. Putting a value in state means “when this changes, the screen should change”. A value that does not affect the screen does not need to be state.
